definitions.explanation: A thin stick of wood, bamboo, or metal used for piercing and holding food for grilling or frying. A staple item in Japanese street food and izakaya cuisine.

examples.japanese: ⟦{屋台|やたい}→屋台：10549_yatai⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{串焼|くしや}き⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{三本|さんぼん}⟦{買|か}った→買う：00489_kau⟧。
examples.english: I bought three skewers of grilled food at a street stall.

examples.japanese: ⟦{串|くし}カツ→串カツ：11354_kushikatsu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{大阪|おおさか}→大阪：09779_oosaka⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{名物|めいぶつ}→名物：05591_meibutsu⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧、{二度漬|にどづ}け⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{禁止|きんし}→禁止：02643_kinshi⟧だ。
examples.english: Kushikatsu is an Osaka specialty, and double-dipping the sauce is forbidden.

notes:
A thin stick used for piercing food, central to many Japanese dishes. Skewered foods are a major category in Japanese cuisine, from yakitori to kushikatsu.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {串|くし}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{刺|さ}す→刺す：02111_sasu⟧ — to thread onto a skewer
- {串焼|くしや}き — skewer-grilled food
- ⟦{串|くし}カツ→串カツ：11354_kushikatsu⟧ — deep-fried skewered cutlets
- ⟦{焼|や}き{鳥|とり}→焼き鳥：04952_yakitori⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{串|くし} — yakitori skewer
- {串|くし}⟦{団子|だんご}→団子：04959_dango⟧ — skewered dango

COUNTING PATTERNS:
Skewered items are counted with {本|ほん} (the counter for long thin objects): ⟦{一本|いっぽん}→一本：08888_ippon⟧、{二本|にほん}、{三本|さんぼん}.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{櫛|くし}→櫛：03882_kushi⟧ — comb (same pronunciation, different kanji and meaning)
- {竹串|たけぐし} — bamboo skewer
- {金串|かなぐし} — metal skewer
